content.text:
## Audit

The markup itself was already solid: the CTA was a real `<button>`, "See what is included" a real `<a href="#details">`, `lang` was set, the viewport allowed zooming, there were no removed focus outlines, and no custom widgets needed ARIA retrofitting. Keyboard operability and focus order were already correct out of the box.

The one substantive defect was **color contrast (WCAG 1.4.3, AA)**. Nearly every piece of body text and the CTA button used very light grays/blues on a white background, all failing the 4.5:1 minimum:

| Element | Old color | Contrast on white |
|---|---|---|
| `.sub` | `#a8adb5` | ~2.25:1 |
| `.plan` | `#b9bec6` | ~1.9:1 |
| `.price small` | `#b0b5bd` | ~2.1:1 |
| `ul` (feature list) | `#9aa0a8` | ~2.5:1 |
| `a.more` | `#9db9f2` | ~2.4:1 |
| `.note` | `#bcc1c8` | ~1.85:1 |
| button text `#fff` on `#86a9ef` | — | ~2.35:1 |

All were well below the required 4.5:1 for normal-size text/UI labels.

## Fix

Darkened these colors while keeping the same hues and relative visual hierarchy (muted secondary text stays visually secondary, the link stays blue, the button stays blue-filled):

- Muted text (`.sub`, `.plan`, `.price small`, `ul`, `.note`) → `#5f6672` (~5.78:1 on white)
- Link (`a.more`) → `#3a5fcd` (~5.68:1 on white)
- Button background (`button`) → `#3f66d0`, kept white text (~5.22:1)

No HTML structure, IDs, `data-track` attributes, or the instrumentation script were touched. Layout, spacing, typography, and hierarchy are unchanged — only the low-contrast shades were deepened enough to clear AA with a comfortable margin.

## Left alone

- Native `<button>` and `<a>` elements — already correctly keyboard-operable and already drive the same mouse/keyboard behavior, so no ARIA or JS changes were needed.
- Default browser focus outlines — never suppressed, so they remain visible; no reason to add custom `:focus` styling.
- The `#details` anchor jump — native fragment-link scrolling behaves identically for mouse and keyboard already, so it was left as-is.
